page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.3xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance configuration provides 12 vCPUs mapped across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, alongside 35 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates vector and cryptographic instruction sets, including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AES-NI.

The primary resource focus of the instance is its memory subsystem, delivering 96.0 GB of RAM, which equates to an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmark data shows uncached large-block memory read bandwidth at 71.39 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 43.14 GB/sec. The instance lacks local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistence, and features a baseline network throughput of 4 Gbps. No dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier execution for parallelized computing and in-memory operations. The instance achieved 10.13 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and recorded a multi-core Geekbench score of 5949.0 along with a PassMark CPU score of 11961.29. In contrast, single-threaded processing exhibits lower throughput, evidenced by weak tier rankings in single-core stress-ng tests (1310.88) and single-threaded gzip compression (22.85 GB/sec).

Given its high memory allocation relative to compute capability, ecs.r6.3xlarge offers balanced cost efficiency for memory-heavy operations rather than single-threaded CPU-bound execution. The instance is well suited for in-memory databases such as Redis, enterprise relational databases, distributed caching layers, and intermediate data processing pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.3xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor based on the x86_64 architecture. Managed via KVM, the instance provides 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores and 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio. It includes support for AVX-512 and AES instructions, while omitting onboard GPUs and local storage in favor of network storage systems operating over a 4 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results reveal mid-range performance for memory-intensive and multi-threaded workloads, yielding 10.13 million operations per second in Redis SET testing and a multi-core Geekbench score of 5949.0. Single-core performance falls into lower benchmark tiers. This instance is best configured for workloads that require significant memory footprints, including in-memory caching platforms, enterprise database management systems, and memory-bound data analysis.
